items.question: Can I combine multiple destinations in one day?
items.answer: Yes! For example, Kuta Mandalika combines easily with Tanjung Aan and Sasak Sade Village, while Tiu Kelep pairs nicely with Senaru or Sembalun.

items.question: What is the easiest way to travel between regions in Lombok?
items.answer: Hiring a private car with a local driver-guide is by far the most comfortable, flexible, and stress-free way to explore the island at your own pace.

items.question: Are roads in Lombok easy to navigate?
items.answer: Main highways are smooth and modern, but access roads to secluded beaches and mountain passes can be steep and winding. Our drivers know every route by heart.

items.question: Do destinations charge entrance or community tickets?
items.answer: Most spots charge small local community entrance fees (usually IDR 10,000–30,000). On all our private day tours, entrance tickets and local guide fees are already fully included.

items.title: Gili Islands
items.name: Gili Islands
items.tagline: Turtles, swings, crystal sea and car-free island bliss
highlights: Snorkel alongside green sea turtles
Iconic Bask underwater sculptures
Golden hour beach swings on Gili T
Cozy cafes & white sand on Gili Air
items.overview: A legendary cluster of three tiny coral islands off Lombok's northwest coast. Gili Trawangan is vibrant with beachfront dining and sunset vistas, Gili Meno offers tranquil seclusion and turtle sanctuaries, while Gili Air combines relaxed social energy with laid-back island living. Best of all: motorized transport is completely forbidden.

spots.title: Turtle Point Reef
spots.desc: A vibrant coral shelf where sea turtles routinely feed in gentle shallow currents.

spots.title: Bask Underwater Sculptures
spots.desc: 48 life-sized human stone statues submerged off Gili Meno, forming an eerie artificial reef.

spots.title: Gili T Sunset Beach
spots.desc: Facing west towards Bali's Mount Agung, famed for beach beanbags, live music, and sea swings.

spots.title: Gili Air Coral Bay
spots.desc: Clear shallow reef right off the sand, perfect for casual snorkeling straight from the beach.

tips: No motorbikes or cars: rent a bicycle for around IDR 50,000/day or walk.
Keep cash handy; some smaller beach warungs and boat captains do not take cards.
Protect reefs by wearing rash guards and reef-safe sunscreen.
Private speedboats depart on your schedule from Teluk Nara or Bangsal harbor.

faq.q: How do I reach the Gili Islands from Lombok?
faq.a: We provide private car pickup to Bangsal or Teluk Nara harbour, then transfer you via private speedboat directly to the island beach in about 15 minutes.

faq.q: Can I visit all three Gilis in one day?
faq.a: Yes! Our private Gili Island Hopping tour visits the best snorkeling spots of Trawangan, Meno, and Air in an easy 8-9 hour day itinerary.

items.title: Kuta Mandalika
items.name: Kuta Mandalika
items.tagline: World-class surf, dramatic coastal hills and powdery turquoise bays
highlights: Panoramic sunset from Bukit Merese
Pepper-grain white sand at Tanjung Aan
Gentle beginner surf waves at Selong Belanak
Vibrant cafe and restaurant strip in town
items.overview: Lombok's southern jewel has evolved from a sleepy fishing hub into an international surfing hotspot and coastal playground. Surrounded by dramatic grassy headlands and sheltered turquoise coves, Mandalika blends authentic island charm with boutique cafes, surf schools, and unforgettable sunset vantage points.

spots.title: Bukit Merese (Merese Hill)
spots.desc: Rolling green bluffs overlooking crescent bays; Lombok's most iconic sunset spot.

spots.title: Tanjung Aan Beach
spots.desc: Unique round 'pepper sand' and tranquil turquoise water framed by sweeping hills.

spots.title: Selong Belanak
spots.desc: Wide, shallow sandy beach with soft rolling waves, famous as the best place to learn surfing.

spots.title: Mawun Beach
spots.desc: A secluded horseshoe-shaped bay of emerald-green water protected by towering headlands.

tips: Located just 25 minutes from Lombok International Airport (LOP), making it a great first or last stop.
Climb Bukit Merese late in the afternoon (around 16:30) for the best sunset light.
Try fresh young coconuts from local beachfront warungs along Tanjung Aan.
Wear sunscreen and bring a sun hat; South Lombok beaches have plenty of sunshine.

faq.q: Is Kuta Mandalika good for non-surfers?
faq.a: Absolutely! The bays are calm for swimming, the coastal hill views are breathtaking, and town is filled with great restaurants and coffee shops.

faq.q: How far is Mandalika from the airport?
faq.a: Only 20 to 25 minutes by private car on smooth modern highways.

items.title: Mount Rinjani
items.name: Mount Rinjani & Sembalun
items.tagline: Majestic volcanic peaks, lush Highland valleys and cloud horizons
highlights: Cool misty air of Sembalun highland valley
Pergasingan Hill sunrise panorama
Colorful mosaic farm terraces & strawberry picking
Majestic views of Indonesia's 2nd highest volcano
items.overview: Towering 3,726 meters above the island, Mount Rinjani is the sacred heart of Lombok. Even if you aren't doing the multi-day trek to the crater lake Segara Anak, the surrounding Sembalun highland plateau offers crisp cool air, patchwork farm fields, strawberry orchards, and accessible viewpoint hills like Pergasingan.

spots.title: Pergasingan Hill
spots.desc: A 2.5-hour hike reward with panoramic views over the colorful Sembalun valley grid.

spots.title: Pusuk Sembalun Viewpoint
spots.desc: High pass viewpoint looking into the volcanic caldera and valley mist.

spots.title: Sembalun Strawberry Farms
spots.desc: Pick fresh strawberries and sweet mountain vegetables straight from local highland plots.

spots.title: Beleq Traditional Village
spots.desc: Ancestral bamboo stilt houses nestled beneath the slopes of the sacred volcano.

tips: Temperatures in Sembalun drop noticeably in the evening; bring a warm fleece or light jacket.
Rinjani National Park trekking routes are closed during the wet season (usually Jan–Mar) for conservation.
Day trips to Sembalun from Senggigi or Kuta take around 2.5 hours each way with our private driver.

faq.q: Can I enjoy Rinjani without a multi-day trek?
faq.a: Yes! Our Sembalun & Rinjani Foothills day tour lets you enjoy the incredible views, Pergasingan hill, and highland farms without camping.

faq.q: What should I wear in Sembalun?
faq.a: Layers! Mornings and evenings can be brisk (15-18°C), while daytime remains pleasantly sunny.

items.title: Pink Beach
items.name: Pink Beach (Tangsi)
items.tagline: Rare rosy coral sand, calm crystalline bays and quiet cliffs
highlights: Pastel pink sand from crushed red organ pipe coral
Climb Tanjung Ringgit cliffs for panoramic ocean views
Calm, child-friendly shallow waters
Boat hopping to uninhabited sandbars
items.overview: Tucked away in the remote southeastern peninsula of Lombok, Pantai Tangsi (famously known as Pink Beach) is one of only a handful of naturally pink-hued beaches on Earth. The delicate pink blush comes from microscopic red organism fragments blending with brilliant white sand.

spots.title: Pink Beach 1 & 2
spots.desc: The primary bays with rosy hues, especially vivid under morning sun and gentle surf.

spots.title: Tanjung Ringgit
spots.desc: Dramatic sheer white limestone cliffs facing the open Indian Ocean and Alas Strait.

spots.title: Gili Petelu
spots.desc: Small uninhabited islets just offshore with untouched coral bommies and clownfish.

spots.title: Pasir Sandbar
spots.desc: A tidal sand island that emerges only at low tide for unforgettable photo stops.

tips: The pink color is most vivid in the morning (around 08:00 - 11:00) when the sun hits the shoreline at an angle.
Combine with boat snorkeling to Gili Petelu and the disappearing sandbar.
The road to East Lombok traverses scenic rural fishing villages and salt evaporation fields.

faq.q: Why is the sand pink?
faq.a: Millions of microscopic red foraminifera shells and dead organ-pipe coral blend with pure white calcium sand.

faq.q: Is Pink Beach accessible by car?
faq.a: Yes! Our private cars drive to Tanjung Luar or straight to the beach, with boat combinations available.

items.title: Tiu Kelep Waterfall
items.name: Tiu Kelep & Sendang Gile
items.tagline: Enchanted rainforest cascades plunging from Rinjani's volcanic springs
highlights: 45m curtain of water rushing into emerald pools
Fun river wading trek through lush rainforest
Easy walk to Sendang Gile first tier
Cool, invigorating volcanic spring water
items.overview: Deep inside the lush jungle foothills of Mount Rinjani near the village of Senaru lie Lombok's most celebrated waterfalls. Sendang Gile cascades in two mighty tiers, while a further 30-minute hike crossing rocky river shallows brings you to Tiu Kelep, where a thundering curtain of spring water creates a magical misty amphitheater.

spots.title: Sendang Gile
spots.desc: A two-tier, 30-meter waterfall reached via a scenic stepped pathway surrounded by monkeys.

spots.title: Tiu Kelep Amphitheater
spots.desc: The main attraction: a horseshoe canyon with a powerful plunge pool and rainbow mists.

spots.title: Senaru Traditional Village
spots.desc: Century-old Sasak heritage village at the base of the mountain trail.

spots.title: Rinjani Foothill Aqueduct
spots.desc: Historic mountain irrigation canal bridge framed by giant ferns and wild banana plants.

tips: Wear sturdy water shoes or sandals with strap grips; you will cross ankle-to-knee-deep rivers.
Bring a dry bag or waterproof pouch for your phone and camera.
Local guide is recommended for safely navigating the river rocks to Tiu Kelep (included in our tours!).

faq.q: How difficult is the hike to Tiu Kelep?
faq.a: Moderate. Sendang Gile is an easy 15-minute walk down stairs. Tiu Kelep is a 30-minute trek involving stepping stones and shallow river crossings.

faq.q: Can you swim under the waterfalls?
faq.a: Yes! The natural pool at the base of Tiu Kelep is fresh and chilly—incredibly refreshing after the hike.

items.title: Secret Gilis Sekotong
items.name: Secret Gilis of Sekotong
items.tagline: Uncrowded sandbars, pristine coral gardens and peaceful Robinson Crusoe vibes
highlights: Tiny uninhabited island of Gili Kedis
Vibrant marine life and soft corals at Gili Nanggu
Grilled fresh fish lunch right on Gili Sudak
Zero beach crowds or boat traffic
items.overview: Far from the bustling northern Gilis, the southwestern peninsula of Sekotong hides a peaceful archipelago of miniature islands: Gili Nanggu, Gili Sudak, and the tiny heart-shaped Gili Kedis. Here, the water is glassy and calm, corals are remarkably healthy, and you can often have an entire sandbar all to yourself.

spots.title: Gili Nanggu Marine Sanctuary
spots.desc: Protected coral reserve where hundreds of colorful damselfish and clownfish surround you.

spots.title: Gili Sudak
spots.desc: A quiet coconut-lined island with peaceful shores and authentic fresh seafood warungs.

spots.title: Gili Kedis
spots.desc: A pint-sized sand island you can walk around in under two minutes, surrounded by turquoise shallows.

spots.title: Sekotong Coastal Road
spots.desc: Scenic coastal drive past tranquil fishing bays and traditional pearl farms.

tips: Bring bread crumbs or fish food (captains often provide it) for an incredible fish-feeding snorkel experience.
Ideal for families with young children or couples seeking total peace.
Boats depart from Tawun harbor in Sekotong, about 1.5 hours drive from Senggigi or Kuta.

faq.q: How do Secret Gilis differ from northern Gilis?
faq.a: Secret Gilis are much quieter, with no parties, fewer boats, pristine corals, and authentic seclusion.

faq.q: Are facilities available on these islands?
faq.a: Gili Sudak has simple restrooms and fresh seafood warungs; Gili Kedis is completely uninhabited and untouched.

items.title: Sade Traditional Sasak Village
items.name: Sade Traditional Sasak Village
items.tagline: Living ancestral hamlet with 150 families, woven bamboo homes and living Sasak customs
highlights: Traditional thatched-roof 'bale tani' homes
Handloom Songket and Ikat textile weaving
Warm hospitality and guided stories by local elders
Traditional Peresean stick-fighting demonstration
items.overview: Step back centuries into the living culture of the indigenous Sasak people. Villages like Sade and Ende preserve traditional architecture with woven bamboo walls, alang-alang thatched roofs, and natural cow-dung treated clay floors. Local women demonstrate intricate traditional weaving passed down across generations.

spots.title: Bale Tani & Bale Lumbung
spots.desc: Distinctive thatched architectural homes and elevated rice barns symbolizing Sasak identity.

spots.title: Songket Weaving Looms
spots.desc: Witness skilled artisans handcrafting intricate ceremonial textiles over months of work.

spots.title: Village Square
spots.desc: Community gathering space where visitors are welcomed with local coffee and cultural explanations.

spots.title: Traditional Handicraft Stalls
spots.desc: Support village families directly by purchasing handmade scarfs, woven bracelets, and pottery.

tips: Modest dress is appreciated out of respect for local customs (shoulders and knees covered).
A local resident guide will escort you through the village alleys; tips or small donations directly support the village fund.
Located right by the airport highway, making it an ideal cultural stop on arrival or departure day.

faq.q: Do people actually still live in Sade?
faq.a: Yes! Around 150 families live here and maintain their ancestral traditions day to day.

faq.q: How long does a visit usually take?
faq.a: A relaxed guided walking tour of the village takes around 1 to 1.5 hours.

items.title: Tetebatu Valleys
items.name: Tetebatu Green Valleys
items.tagline: Emerald rice terraces, misty clove forests and Black Monkey sanctuaries
highlights: Panoramic step rice terraces overlooking Rinjani
Spot rare endemic Javan Langur (Black Monkeys)
Walk through organic coffee, clove, and vanilla plantations
Sarang Walet (Swallow Cave) hidden waterfall
items.overview: Often described as 'what Ubud was 30 years ago', Tetebatu is an enchanting rural village perched on the southern slopes of Mount Rinjani. Surrounded by tiered green rice paddies, spice plantations, and cooling jungle streams, it represents the tranquil rural soul of Lombok.

spots.title: Tetebatu Rice Terraces
spots.desc: Spectacular amphitheater of lush green paddies with Mount Rinjani rising in the background.

spots.title: Monkey Forest Sanctuary
spots.desc: Protected highland jungle home to shy, rare Black Leaf Langurs and gray macaques.

spots.title: Sarang Walet Waterfall
spots.desc: A hidden cavern waterfall flowing through narrow mossy rock gorges.

spots.title: Spice & Coffee Groves
spots.desc: Taste freshly roasted Lombok Robusta and learn how vanilla, nutmeg, and cloves grow.

tips: Bring good walking shoes or light trainers for the gentle 2-hour paddy and plantation trek.
Tetebatu stays significantly cooler than the coastal towns—bring a light sweater for evening walks.
Enjoy a cup of locally grown organic coffee at an open-air bamboo warung overlooking the paddies.

faq.q: Is Tetebatu suitable for casual walkers?
faq.a: Yes! The walking routes through the rice paddies and village paths are gentle and suitable for all fitness levels.

faq.q: Can I visit Tetebatu on a day trip?
faq.a: Yes, our driver-guides can comfortably take you to Tetebatu from Senggigi, Mataram, or Kuta for a day trip.

items.title: Selong Belanak Beach
items.name: Selong Belanak Beach
items.tagline: Soft crescent white sands, gentle waves for beginner surf, and sunset buffalo parades
highlights: Lombok's premier beach for beginner surf lessons
Wide sweeping bay of velvety soft white sand
Local fishermen & picturesque sunset water buffalo strolls
Beachside fresh coconut warungs and bamboo loungers
items.overview: Selong Belanak is universally celebrated as Lombok's friendliest beach. Tucked into an expansive sheltered crescent bay in South Lombok, its turquoise waters roll into gentle sandy-bottom breaks that make it the ultimate learning ground for surfing beginners. In late afternoon, local farmers slowly herd their water buffalo across the shoreline, creating an iconic, peaceful Lombok postcard.

spots.title: Beginner Surf Break
spots.desc: Mellow foam and soft sandy bottom with local certified instructors ready on the sand.

spots.title: Buffalo Sunset Shoreline
spots.desc: Iconic daily evening walk of water buffalo strolling across the gleaming low-tide wet sand.

spots.title: Coconut Warung Promenade
spots.desc: Chilled young coconuts, fresh grilled fish, and surfboard rental shacks lining the palm tree shade.

spots.title: Western Point Lookout
spots.desc: Gentle headland trail offering panoramic views across the full crescent bay.

tips: Surfing lessons cost around IDR 250,000 to 350,000 including 2 hours coaching and board hire.
Water shoes are not needed here—the entire sea floor is silky smooth sand with zero sea urchins.
Stay for the sunset around 18:00 when the buffalo parade takes place.

faq.q: Is Selong Belanak safe for young children?
faq.a: Yes! Unlike some heavy reef breaks in South Lombok, Selong Belanak has gentle shallow waters with no dangerous drop-offs.

faq.q: Can I visit Selong Belanak on a beach hopping day tour?
faq.a: Yes! It pairs seamlessly with Mawun Beach, Kuta Mandalika, and Tanjung Aan on our South Lombok Beach Tour.

items.title: Ende Traditional Sasak Village
items.name: Ende Traditional Sasak Village
items.tagline: Intimate Sasak hamlet of thatched lumbung houses, authentic tribal customs, and rich folklore
highlights: Authentic living Sasak community of around 30 families
Distinctive Bale Tani architecture built with clay, bamboo & thatch
Intimate guided walking tours led directly by community elders
Live demonstration of Peresean stick-and-shield martial arts
items.overview: Desa Ende is a beautifully preserved indigenous Sasak hamlet situated just a short drive from Lombok International Airport. Quieter and more intimate than neighboring Sade, Ende is home to about thirty families who choose to live in traditional clay-and-cow-dung floor houses with alang-alang thatched roofs, keeping ancestral customs and rituals vibrantly alive without modern electricity.

spots.title: Bale Tani & Bale Kodong
spots.desc: Traditional single-room dwelling built according to sacred Sasak directional principles.

spots.title: Lumbung Rice Barns
spots.desc: Elevated wooden granaries with round wooden caps designed to prevent rodents from climbing.

spots.title: Ende Village Arena
spots.desc: Central courtyard where ceremonial Peresean (rattan stick fighting) demonstrations are staged.

spots.title: Weaving Shacks
spots.desc: Village women hand-spinning cotton and naturally dyeing threads for vibrant songket cloths.

tips: Visits are guided by a village resident; a voluntary community donation (usually IDR 50k–100k) is customary.
Ask your guide about the unique clay-and-buffalo-dung floor tradition that naturally repels mosquitoes and dust.
Photography is welcome and locals are warm, but always ask before photographing elders inside their homes.

faq.q: What is the difference between Sade and Ende?
faq.a: Sade is larger and more famous (around 150 families), whereas Ende is smaller, quieter, and feels very personal and intimate.

faq.q: Is Ende easily accessible on arrival or departure?
faq.a: Yes! It is located only 15 minutes from Lombok Airport, making it the perfect stop right after landing or before a flight.

items.title: Tanjung Aan Beach & Merese Hill
items.name: Tanjung Aan Beach & Merese Hill
items.tagline: Pepper-grain white sand, calm turquoise swimming lagoons, and sweeping cliff sunsets
highlights: Unique round pepper-sized sand grains along the wide shoreline
Sheltered double-curve bay perfect for swimming & SUP paddleboarding
Iconic Merese Hill panoramic ridge walk overlooking the Indian Ocean
Lombok's most celebrated sunset viewpoint
items.overview: Tanjung Aan is widely considered the crown jewel of South Lombok's beaches. Known for its remarkable sand with grains resembling tiny white peppercorns, this sweeping double-crescent bay features calm, crystalline turquoise waters flanked by Bukit Merese (Merese Hill). Climbing the gentle green hill at golden hour treats visitors to a 360-degree dramatic cliff vista as the sunset turns the sea molten gold.

spots.title: Merese Sunset Ridge
spots.desc: A gentle 10-minute grassy walk to headland cliffs overlooking dramatic crashing ocean waves.

spots.title: Pepper Sand Shoreline
spots.desc: Rare geological sand formation of tiny smooth calcite pellets that feel delightful underfoot.

spots.title: Batu Payung View
spots.desc: Secluded eastern headland looking toward the iconic sea-sculpted rock formations.

spots.title: Turquoise Swimming Lagoon
spots.desc: Protected bay with gentle current, ideal for floating, swimming, and kayaking.

tips: Climb Bukit Merese about 45 minutes before sunset (around 17:15) to find the best perch on the cliff edge.
Bring cash for coconut warungs and small entrance/parking fees (IDR 10k–15k).
Wear sunglasses and sunscreen during the midday heat as there is minimal natural shade along the open beach.

faq.q: Is the hike up Merese Hill difficult?
faq.a: Not at all; it is a gentle 10-minute grassy path suitable for travelers of any age and fitness level.

faq.q: Can we swim at Tanjung Aan?
faq.a: Yes! Unlike some surf breaks nearby, Tanjung Aan's inner bay is calm and excellent for relaxed swimming.

items.title: Benang Kelambu & Stokel Waterfalls
items.name: Benang Kelambu & Stokel Waterfalls
items.tagline: Spring water cascading like sheer curtains through lush cliff foliage on Rinjani's slope
items.vibe: Living Curtain of Fresh Spring Water
highlights: Unique "curtain" waterfall flowing directly through dense living jungle vines
Twin 30-meter free-falling cascades of Benang Stokel
Natural swimming basins filled with pure mountain spring water
Scenic paved walking path through coffee and fruit plantations
items.overview: Nestled on the southwestern slopes of Mount Rinjani in Central Lombok, Benang Kelambu and Benang Stokel are among Indonesia's most unusual and magical waterfalls. While Benang Stokel features dramatic twin chutes tumbling down a 30-meter sheer rock face, Benang Kelambu looks like a fairytale: pure mountain spring water emerges directly from forest cliffs and drapes down tiers of leafy climbing vines like a lace mosquito net ("kelambu").

spots.title: Benang Kelambu Living Curtain
spots.desc: Multi-tiered waterfall cascading through a lush tapestry of ferns and wild river vines.

spots.title: Benang Stokel Twin Chutes
spots.desc: Powerful twin waterfall plunging into a natural refreshing splash pool.

spots.title: Bat Cave & Spring Stream
spots.desc: Shaded jungle creek where fresh mountain water flows toward village irrigation canals.

spots.title: Coffee & Durian Orchard Trail
spots.desc: Shady mountain trail lined with coffee shrubs, jackfruit, and towering tropical trees.

tips: Bring a change of dry clothes and swimwear—standing under the gentle spray of Kelambu feels incredible.
A local guide is included at the park entrance to guide your walking route safely.
Optional local motorcycle taxi (ojek) is available if you prefer not to walk the 15-minute paved route back up.

faq.q: How long is the walk to both waterfalls?
faq.a: Benang Stokel is an easy 10-minute walk from the gate. Benang Kelambu is another 15 minutes along a paved footpath.

faq.q: Is this waterfall safe for kids and seniors?
faq.a: Yes! Paved footpaths and handrails make this one of the most accessible waterfall sites in all of Lombok.

items.title: Mawun Beach
items.name: Mawun Beach
items.tagline: Secluded horseshoe-shaped bay protected by twin rolling headlands with cerulean waters
highlights: Distinctive horseshoe-shaped enclosed bay flanked by green mountain headlands
Dramatic gradient of sea colors from neon turquoise to deep sapphire blue
Soft blonde sand and gentle sea breeze under solitary shade trees
Less crowded and commercialized than Kuta center
items.overview: Mawun Beach is an enchanting, almost symmetrical horseshoe-shaped bay located between Selong Belanak and Kuta. Guarded on both sides by prominent green conical hills, the bay forms an amphitheater of calm waters near the edges and thrilling deeper swimming in the center. It remains one of the south coast's best-kept secrets for travelers seeking peace away from beach bars.

spots.title: Eastern Headland Lookout
spots.desc: A short scenic scramble up the grassy hill providing an aerial view of the full crescent cove.

spots.title: Central Deep Lagoon
spots.desc: Deep cerulean swimming area for confident swimmers with breathtaking ocean water clarity.

spots.title: Shaded Tree Hammocks
spots.desc: Tranquil shoreline under large trees where local vendors offer cold drinks and fresh fruit.

tips: The sea drops off into deep water fairly quickly in the middle of the bay—swimmers should stay attentive to currents.
The edges near the flanking headlands offer the calmest, shallowest swimming waters.
Grab a fresh young coconut and freshly grilled corn from the local beach stalls.

faq.q: Is Mawun close to Selong Belanak?
faq.a: Yes! It is just a 15-minute scenic drive along the coastal road between Kuta Mandalika and Selong Belanak.

items.title: Sukarara Hand-Weaving Village
items.name: Sukarara Hand-Weaving Village
items.tagline: Living masterweavers crafting intricate Songket and Ikat textiles on antique wooden looms
highlights: Watch master Sasak craftswomen weaving Songket with gold and silver metallic threads
Hands-on experience sitting at an antique wooden backstrap loom
Try on traditional Sasak royal wedding costumes for free souvenir photos
Direct-from-artisan authentic handwoven scarves, sarongs and table runners
items.overview: Sukarara is Lombok's world-famous textile village where every daughter learns the intricate art of weaving before marriage. As you walk through the village, the gentle rhythmic clicking of wooden looms echoes from open verandas. Master weavers spend anywhere from three weeks to several months creating a single piece of Sasak Songket or Ikat, embedding geometric motifs, ancestral symbols, and natural plant dyes.

spots.title: Weaving Veranda Workshops
spots.desc: Open-air village looms where multiple generations of women weave side by side.

spots.title: Sasak Costume Photo Studio
spots.desc: Complimentary dress-up in regal Sasak attire in front of a traditional thatched rice barn.

spots.title: Natural Dye Garden
spots.desc: Display of native plants used for coloration: betel nut for red, indigo for blue, and bark for rich browns.

tips: Visitors are welcomed to dress up in colorful Sasak royal outfits for memorable photos at no extra cost.
Buying a handwoven scarf directly from the weaver provides vital livelihood support to village families.
Feel free to sit at the loom and try pushing the shuttle across the threads—the artisans love to teach you.

faq.q: How long does a visit to Sukarara take?
faq.a: Typically 45 to 60 minutes, which includes watching the weaving, trying the loom, and taking costume photos.

items.overview: Standing 1,750 meters above sea level right across the valley from Mount Rinjani, Pergasingan Hill is celebrated as the premier viewpoint hike in Lombok. The climb ascends rocky stairs and mountain trails through high savannah grass to reach a summit plateau where clouds pool like an ocean at dawn. Looking down reveals the breathtaking geometric kaleidoscope of Sembalun's vegetable and strawberry fields below.

spots.title: Valley Farmland Viewpoint

tips: The hike takes approximately 2 to 2.5 hours from the base to the summit rim.
Nighttime summit temperatures can drop to 12°C—bring warm fleece, windproof jacket, and headlamp.
Our 2D1N camping package includes porters who carry your tents, sleeping bags, and cook warm meals.

faq.a: A moderate level of fitness is recommended. The trail has steep stair sections at the start, followed by manageable ridge paths.

items.overview: Lombok's capital city Mataram is a fascinating crossroads of ancient kingdoms and modern island life. Explore Mayura Palace, a serene 1744 royal courtroom floating in a water reservoir surrounded by mangosteen trees. At Narmada Park, discover the 18th-century King of Mataram's recreation palace and drink from the natural spring believed to grant eternal youth, then visit the soaring minarets of the Grand Islamic Center.
